classificationCases.case: A durable research Task reached terminal completed state. It produced no artifact and no claim about world consequence was evaluated.
A tool-building Task completed, produced a correct instrument, and the declared objective was exactly to construct that instrument. Nobody has used it downstream yet.
An experiment failed its original performance objective, but unexpectedly revealed and independently verified a previously unknown safety failure that changes future design decisions.
A later named consumer demonstrably uses a research artifact in its ordinary workflow. No beneficial or adverse downstream consequence has yet been observed.

A named downstream consumer used a change; compared with the frozen prior baseline under the same workload and constraints, its verified error rate fell with no protected-consequence regression. Attribution to the change is independently supported for that bounded consumer/horizon.

A dormant capability is not currently used, but a source-fenced analysis establishes a plausible future family where reacquisition would be costly and retaining it preserves a concrete option. No later use or benefit has occurred.
System B improves one benchmark score over A, but a protected consequence regresses and the comparison scope did not include that consequence.

Within an explicitly declared comparison scope, B weakly dominates A on every protected consequence and strictly improves at least one, under the same relevant constraints and horizon. The broader feasible/search space is not characterized.

For a finite declared feasible set and explicit objective, every feasible alternative has been evaluated under the same valid evidence bridge and candidate X is best. Nothing is claimed outside that envelope.
A new benchmark apparatus runs correctly and now makes a previously unmeasurable hypothesis testable; the hypothesis has not yet been tested.
A later document cites and links an earlier research result, but its decision rule is unchanged and no evidence shows the earlier result causally entered the decision.
A consumer's practice matches a research recommendation, but version history proves the practice existed before the research and continued unchanged afterward.

transferCases.case: A team finished 80 experiments and produced 80 reports. Ten independently changed a declared decision boundary; the rest were null, redundant, or only supporting material. Which public claim is justified?
A new Agent tool is callable and has been invoked in one workflow, but there is no observed downstream performance, cost, reliability, or beneficiary change. Which product statement is justified?
A benchmark rises 12%, while a protected failure-recovery rate worsens. Product leadership asks whether to announce 'the system improved'.

A falsification campaign disproves the current preferred design and rules out a costly implementation path. Its declared research objective was to resolve whether that path should be built. What should the closeout say?

An external operator adopts a component and reports lower incident recovery time; logs and a frozen before/after design support attribution for that operator and quarter, but no other user has been measured. What may be claimed?

A research team builds a new sensor specifically to test whether a suspected phenomenon exists. The sensor passes calibration, but the phenomenon experiment has not run. Should the hypothesis be promoted?

A dormant adapter has no current consumer. Retaining it costs almost nothing; rebuilding it later is costly; a concrete future integration family is plausible but uncertain. What is the strongest justified decision?

A review task's only objective is to decide whether a public page must change after an owner revision. Revalidation shows all reader-relevant standing unchanged, so the decision is NO_OP. How should task success be judged?
A team has fully evaluated every option in a deliberately finite procurement shortlist under a declared cost/reliability objective and selects the best option. How should it word the result?
A downstream codebase contains the same pattern recommended by a research report, but Git proves the pattern predates the report. Should the report be credited as consumed by that codebase?
